findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. a logged-in user navigating directly to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never visited or been notified about). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level` on this possibly-nil value, which raises `NoMethodError` and results in a 500 error instead of a handled response. The code should use `TopicUser.change`/`TopicUser.find_or_create_by` or otherwise guard against a missing record.

findings.title: unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change, losing MessageBus publish and reason/changed_at bookkeeping
findings.body: Instead of calling the existing `TopicUser.change` class method (used everywhere else notification_level is modified, e.g. in `set_notifications`), this action mutates the `TopicUser` record directly and calls `tu.save!`. This skips setting `notifications_changed_at` / `notifications_reason_id`, and skips the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... })` call that other sessions/tabs rely on to update the UI live. The result is inconsistent bookkeeping and stale notification icons in any other open browser tab/session for the same user.

findings.title: Per-topic unsubscribe mutates state on a plain, login-gated GET request
findings.body: Unlike the existing digest unsubscribe flow (`email/unsubscribe/:key`, backed by `DigestUnsubscribeKey`) which works without an active login session via a signed token, this new `unsubscribe` action requires `ensure_logged_in` and performs the notification-level mutation synchronously on a GET request tied to the user's session cookie. This both breaks the "click unsubscribe from any device/mail client" use case the digest flow supports, and is a state-changing GET endpoint driven purely by session cookies, which is a classic CSRF-prone pattern (an embedded image/link while the victim is logged in elsewhere in the same browser would silently flip their notification level).

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url but builder doesn't guarantee it's present
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` locale string was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml). `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, but `unsubscribe_url` is an optional opt with no default/fallback. Only `send_notification_email` in `user_notifications.rb` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other current or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will hit `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to build the email entirely.

findings.title: Template location likely mismatches the route/controller naming convention
findings.body: The route is registered as a top-level route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', {...})` in app-route-map.js.es6 (not nested inside the `topic` resource), and its controller/view are named `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` (flat, dasherized). By Ember's naming convention this route resolves its template as `topic-unsubscribe` (flat), not the nested path `topic/unsubscribe` used here. Other nested routes in this codebase (e.g. `topic.fromParams`) use the `topic/...` template path precisely because they are declared inside `this.resource('topic', ...)`. Since `topicUnsubscribe` is not nested, placing the template at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` will likely fail to resolve, leaving the route's outlet blank at runtime.

findings.title: Misspelled computed property name "stopNotificiationsText"
findings.body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing an "a", should be "Notifications"). It is functionally consistent with its one use in the template, so it isn't a runtime bug, but the typo will confuse future maintainers searching the codebase and should be fixed before merge.

findings.title: No test coverage added for the new unsubscribe controller/model behavior
findings.body: This PR adds substantial new server-side behavior (`TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `Topic#unsubscribe_url`) but the only test change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` opt to an existing MessageBuilder spec. There is no controller spec exercising `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (including the nil-TopicUser case, the slug-redirect branch, or the notification-level toggle logic), and no spec verifying `Topic#unsubscribe_url`. Given the nil-TopicUser crash risk identified elsewhere in this review, test coverage for this action would have caught the bug before merge.
